subject: psychology
title: Multi-Store Model: Architecture
welcome_lead: Atkinson & Shiffrin's blueprint for human memory.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology Multi-Store Model Atkinson & Shiffrin 1968 sensory STM LTM.
final_note: Three stores in a line — simple, testable, falsifiable.

concepts.def: Maintenance process moving info from STM to LTM.

walkthroughs.body_html: Atkinson & Shiffrin (1968) proposed three stores in sequence. Information enters via sensory register; attention transfers it to STM; rehearsal transfers it to LTM. Without attention, sensory info decays; without rehearsal, STM info is lost.

Sperling (1960): participants briefly shown 12-letter grids. Whole-report recall ~4 letters; partial report (cued by tone immediately) ~9 letters. Sensory register holds large capacity but decays in ~250ms (iconic). Echoic memory lasts a few seconds longer.

STM has limited capacity and duration. Maintenance rehearsal keeps info in STM by recycling; elaborative rehearsal links to existing LTM, deepening the trace (Craik & Lockhart 1972). Both transfer to LTM, but elaborative is more effective.
